feedback.incorrectEs: Observa el resultado positivo y el contraste introducido por “although”.

activities.title: Resolve a reference

feedback.incorrect: Look at the noun in the previous sentence that caused the change.
feedback.incorrectEs: Busca el sustantivo de la oración anterior que produjo el cambio.

The team moved the sensor away from direct sunlight.
As a result, the readings became more stable.

feedback.correct: Correct. The sequence moves from problem to action to result.
feedback.correctEs: Correcto. La secuencia pasa del problema a la acción y luego al resultado.
feedback.incorrect: Look for the problem first, the action second, and the result last.
feedback.incorrectEs: Busca primero el problema, después la acción y al final el resultado.

activities.title: Ask a follow-up question
activities.prompt: A colleague says, “The first test failed.” Which response keeps the conversation going?
activities.promptEs: Un compañero dice: “La primera prueba falló”. ¿Qué respuesta mantiene la conversación?
options: What do you think caused it?
activities.answer: What do you think caused it?

feedback.correct: Correct. A follow-up question invites more information.
feedback.correctEs: Correcto. Una pregunta de seguimiento invita a ampliar la información.
feedback.incorrect: Choose a question connected to what your colleague said.
feedback.incorrectEs: Elige una pregunta relacionada con lo que dijo tu compañero.

spiralReview.retrievalCue: Extend basic questions into meaningful follow-up questions.

activities.title: Disagree politely
activities.prompt: “I see your point, ___ I think we should test it again.”
activities.promptEs: “Entiendo tu punto, ___ creo que deberíamos probarlo otra vez”.

feedback.correct: Correct. Acknowledging the other view before disagreeing keeps the tone respectful.
feedback.correctEs: Correcto. Reconocer la otra opinión antes de discrepar mantiene un tono respetuoso.
feedback.incorrect: Use a contrast connector after acknowledging the other person's view.
feedback.incorrectEs: Usa un conector de contraste después de reconocer la opinión de la otra persona.

activities.title: Respond to an idea
activities.prompt: Put the conversation in a natural order.
activities.promptEs: Pon la conversación en un orden natural.

Good point. We should compare both conditions.
answer: I think the sensor needs more light.
That makes sense. What if we test it outdoors too?
Good point. We should compare both conditions.

feedback.correct: Correct. The exchange presents an idea, reacts to it, and adds a next step.
feedback.correctEs: Correcto. El intercambio presenta una idea, reacciona y añade un siguiente paso.
feedback.incorrect: Start with the idea, respond to it, and then suggest the next step.
feedback.incorrectEs: Empieza con la idea, responde a ella y luego propone el siguiente paso.

activities.title: Reported Speech: recognise the speaker
activities.prompt: Mia says, “Hello!” What does Mia do?
activities.promptEs: Mia dice: «¡Hola!». ¿Qué hace Mia?

feedback.correct: Correct. You are identifying the message, not changing its grammar yet.
feedback.correctEs: Correcto. Identificas el mensaje; todavía no cambias la gramática.
feedback.incorrect: Choose the option that describes Mia's message.
feedback.incorrectEs: Elige la opción que describe el mensaje de Mia.

activities.prompt: Match the direct message with its report.
activities.promptEs: Relaciona el mensaje directo con lo que se cuenta.

Tom says, “Thanks!” → Tom asks for help.
activities.answer: Tom says, “Thanks!” → Tom says thank you.

feedback.correct: Correct. The reported message keeps the original meaning.
feedback.correctEs: Correcto. El mensaje transmitido conserva el sentido original.
feedback.incorrect: Look for the option that keeps the meaning of “Thanks!”.
feedback.incorrectEs: Busca la opción que conserva el significado de «Thanks!».

activities.title: Reported Speech: understand a short message
activities.titleEs: Estilo indirecto: comprende un mensaje breve
activities.prompt: Imagine you hear: “Ben says he is at home.” What do you know?
activities.promptEs: Imagina que escuchas: «Ben dice que está en casa». ¿Qué sabes?
options: Ben says he is at home.
Ben says he is at school.
activities.answer: Ben says he is at home.

feedback.correct: Correct. Identify who the message is about and what it says.
feedback.correctEs: Correcto. Identifica de quién trata el mensaje y qué dice.
feedback.incorrect: Choose the option with the same information.
feedback.incorrectEs: Elige la opción que contiene la misma información.

activities.audioText: Ben says he is at home.

activities.title: Reported Speech: pass on a greeting
activities.prompt: Put the short exchange in a natural order.
activities.promptEs: Ordena el intercambio breve de forma natural.

feedback.correct: Correct. A simple report tells another person the message.
feedback.correctEs: Correcto. Un reporte sencillo transmite el mensaje a otra persona.
feedback.incorrect: Start with the question, then give Anna's message and report it.
feedback.incorrectEs: Empieza con la pregunta, después presenta el mensaje de Anna y transmítelo.

activities.title: Reported Speech: statements with said
activities.prompt: Direct: “I am tired,” Mia said. Choose the usual past-time report.
activities.promptEs: Directo: «Estoy cansada», dijo Mia. Elige la forma indirecta habitual en pasado.
options: Mia said that she was tired.
Mia said that I am tired.
Mia told that she was tired.
activities.answer: Mia said that she was tired.

feedback.correct: After said in the past, am often shifts to was; I changes to she because Mia is reporting about herself.
feedback.correctEs: Después de said en pasado, am suele cambiar a was; I cambia a she porque Mia habla de sí misma.
feedback.incorrect: Check the reporting verb, pronoun and tense.
feedback.incorrectEs: Revisa el verbo introductorio, el pronombre y el tiempo verbal.

activities.title: Reported Speech: preserve meaning
activities.prompt: Choose the report that keeps the original meaning: “We live here,” they said.
activities.promptEs: Elige la versión que conserva el significado: «Vivimos aquí», dijeron.
options: They said that they lived there.
They said that we live here.
activities.answer: They said that they lived there.

feedback.correct: Pronouns and place words may change when the speaker and location change.
feedback.correctEs: Los pronombres y las expresiones de lugar pueden cambiar si cambia el hablante o la ubicación.
feedback.incorrect: Keep the original meaning and consider who is speaking.
feedback.incorrectEs: Conserva el sentido original y considera quién habla.

activities.title: Reported Speech: report a plan
activities.prompt: You hear: “I will call you,” Alex said. What is the usual report?
activities.promptEs: Escuchas: «Te llamaré», dijo Alex. ¿Cuál es la forma indirecta habitual?
options: Alex said that he would call me.
Alex said that he will called me.
Alex told that he would call me.
activities.answer: Alex said that he would call me.

feedback.correct: Will commonly changes to would in reported speech; pronouns depend on who reports the message.
feedback.correctEs: Will suele cambiar a would en estilo indirecto; los pronombres dependen de quién transmite el mensaje.
feedback.incorrect: Check will → would and use said without an object, or told with one.
feedback.incorrectEs: Revisa will → would y usa said sin objeto o told con objeto.

activities.title: Reported Speech: complete a statement
activities.prompt: “I work at a hospital,” he said. → He said that he ___ at a hospital.
activities.promptEs: «Trabajo en un hospital», dijo él. → He said that he ___ at a hospital.

feedback.correct: Work commonly shifts to worked after a past reporting verb.
feedback.correctEs: Work suele cambiar a worked después de un verbo introductorio en pasado.
feedback.incorrect: Use the past form in this typical backshift pattern.
feedback.incorrectEs: Usa la forma de pasado en este patrón habitual de cambio temporal.

activities.title: Reported Speech: indirect questions
activities.prompt: Direct: “Where do you live?” he asked me. Choose the report.
activities.promptEs: Directo: «¿Dónde vives?», me preguntó. Elige la versión indirecta.
options: He asked me where I lived.
He asked me where did I live.
He said me where I lived.
activities.answer: He asked me where I lived.

feedback.correct: Indirect questions use statement word order; do not keep do-support inversion.
feedback.correctEs: Las preguntas indirectas usan el orden de una afirmación; no conservan la inversión con do.
feedback.incorrect: Use question word + subject + verb, and asked for a question.
feedback.incorrectEs: Usa palabra interrogativa + sujeto + verbo, y asked para introducir una pregunta.

activities.title: Reported Speech: report a request
activities.prompt: Match: “Please open the window,” Ana said to me.
activities.promptEs: Relaciona: «Por favor, abre la ventana», me dijo Ana.
options: Ana asked me to open the window.
Ana said me open the window.
Ana asked that I opened the window.
activities.answer: Ana asked me to open the window.

feedback.correct: A common pattern for requests is ask + person + to + base verb.
feedback.correctEs: Un patrón frecuente para peticiones es ask + persona + to + verbo base.
feedback.incorrect: Use asked + object + to + infinitive.
feedback.incorrectEs: Usa asked + objeto + to + infinitivo.

activities.title: Reported Speech: recount an interview
activities.prompt: Put the interview report in a logical order.
activities.promptEs: Ordena el reporte de la entrevista de forma lógica.
options: I reported that she wanted to study law.
She said, “I want to study law.”
The interviewer asked what she wanted to study.
tokens: I reported that she wanted to study law.
She said, “I want to study law.”
The interviewer asked what she wanted to study.
answer: The interviewer asked what she wanted to study.
She said, “I want to study law.”
I reported that she wanted to study law.

feedback.correct: A report introduces the question, records the answer and then summarises it.
feedback.correctEs: Un reporte introduce la pregunta, registra la respuesta y después la resume.
feedback.incorrect: Begin with the interviewer's question, then the answer, then your report.
feedback.incorrectEs: Empieza con la pregunta, sigue con la respuesta y termina con tu reporte.

activities.title: Reported Speech: report advice
activities.prompt: “You should rest,” the doctor said to Leo. → The doctor advised Leo ___ rest.
activities.promptEs: «Deberías descansar», le dijo el médico a Leo. → The doctor advised Leo ___ rest.

feedback.correct: Advise + object + to-infinitive is a common way to report advice.
feedback.correctEs: Advise + objeto + infinitivo con to es una forma frecuente de transmitir consejos.
feedback.incorrect: Use the infinitive marker to after advised + object.
feedback.incorrectEs: Usa to antes del infinitivo después de advised + objeto.

activities.title: Reported Speech: identify the message
activities.prompt: Mia says, “Good morning!” What is the message doing?
activities.promptEs: Mia dice: «¡Buenos días!». ¿Qué función tiene el mensaje?

feedback.correct: A greeting can be reported by naming its function.
feedback.correctEs: Un saludo puede transmitirse indicando su función.
feedback.incorrect: Choose what Mia communicates.
feedback.incorrectEs: Elige lo que comunica Mia.

activities.promptEs: Escucha y elige el mensaje que oyes.

Lina says she is at school.

feedback.incorrect: Listen for the place, “at home”.
feedback.incorrectEs: Escucha el lugar, «at home».

Leo said that I work here.
Leo told that he worked here.

feedback.incorrectEs: Usa he para Leo y there para el otro lugar.

activities.title: Reported Speech: relay a message

Maya said I couldn't attend that day.

feedback.incorrect: Keep Maya as the person who cannot attend.

activities.title: Reported Speech: indirect question order

activities.prompt: Direct: “Where does Nina work?” he asked. Choose the report.
activities.promptEs: Directo: «¿Dónde trabaja Nina?», preguntó él. Elige el reporte.

feedback.incorrectEs: Pon el sujeto antes del verbo: Nina worked.

activities.title: Report a past statement
activities.prompt: Direct: “I have finished my homework,” Sara said. Choose the usual report.
activities.promptEs: Directo: «He terminado mi tarea», dijo Sara. Elige la versión indirecta habitual.
options: Sara said that she had finished her homework.
Sara said that she has finished my homework.
Sara told that she finished her homework.
activities.answer: Sara said that she had finished her homework.

feedback.correct: Correct. With a past reporting verb, present perfect commonly shifts to past perfect: have finished → had finished. “My” changes to “her” because Sara is the speaker.
feedback.correctEs: Correcto. Con un verbo introductorio en pasado, el presente perfecto suele pasar a pasado perfecto: have finished → had finished. “My” cambia a “her” porque Sara es quien habla.
feedback.incorrect: Check two changes: have finished usually becomes had finished, and my must refer to Sara, so use her.
feedback.incorrectEs: Revisa dos cambios: have finished suele convertirse en had finished y my se refiere a Sara, por eso se usa her.

activities.title: Report a future plan
activities.prompt: “We will send the file tomorrow,” they said. → They said they ___ send the file the next day.
activities.promptEs: «Enviaremos el archivo mañana», dijeron. → Dijeron que ___ enviar el archivo al día siguiente.

feedback.correct: Correct. Will commonly changes to would after said in the past. Tomorrow changes to the next day when the reporting time is later.
feedback.correctEs: Correcto. Will suele cambiar a would después de said en pasado. Tomorrow cambia a the next day cuando se transmite el mensaje más tarde.
feedback.incorrect: Use would after said, not will, in the usual backshift pattern: will → would.
feedback.incorrectEs: Usa would después de said en pasado, no will, siguiendo el cambio temporal habitual: will → would.

activities.title: Report a place and time
activities.prompt: Direct: “I am staying here today,” Leo said. You report it tomorrow from another place. Choose the best option.
activities.promptEs: Directo: «Me quedo aquí hoy», dijo Leo. Lo cuentas mañana desde otro lugar. Elige la mejor opción.
options: Leo said that he was staying there that day.
Leo said that I am staying here today.
Leo told that he stayed there tomorrow.
activities.answer: Leo said that he was staying there that day.

feedback.correct: Correct. Am staying commonly shifts to was staying; here becomes there and today becomes that day because the reporting context changed.
feedback.correctEs: Correcto. Am staying suele cambiar a was staying; here pasa a there y today a that day porque cambió el contexto desde el que se cuenta.
feedback.incorrect: Check the speaker, tense and context words: I → he, am staying → was staying, here → there, today → that day.
feedback.incorrectEs: Revisa quién habla, el tiempo y las expresiones de contexto: I → he, am staying → was staying, here → there, today → that day.

activities.title: Choose said or told
activities.prompt: “I need help,” Omar said to me. → Omar ___ me that he needed help.
activities.promptEs: «Necesito ayuda», me dijo Omar. → Omar ___ que necesitaba ayuda.

feedback.correct: Correct. Use told + person: told me. Said does not take the listener directly without “to” (said to me).
feedback.correctEs: Correcto. Usa told + persona: told me. Said no lleva directamente a la persona que escucha sin “to” (said to me).
feedback.incorrect: Because the listener “me” follows the verb, use told: told me. Another correct pattern is said to me.
feedback.incorrectEs: Como después del verbo aparece la persona que escucha (“me”), usa told: told me. Otra estructura correcta es said to me.
